rules: No generic sans-serif for main titles.
Year text must be massive, clamped between text-[8rem] and text-[16rem], tracking-tighter, with high contrast.
Data labels and stats text must be uppercase Space Mono, extremely crisp (10px - 12px) with wide tracking (tracking-[0.1em]).

visual_enhancers.overlays: Use aggressive gradients: bg-gradient-to-r from-transparent via-[#080808]/80 to-[#080808] to blend the left-side image into the right-side data panel seamlessly.
visual_enhancers.textures: Incorporate an SVG noise overlay (mix-blend-overlay, opacity 20%) globally across the component to kill digital flatness and give a raw museum/archival feel.
visual_enhancers.blend_modes: Apply mix-blend-difference or exclusion on overlapping huge typography over images to create tension and artistic immersion.

grids.desktop: Split screen. 60% Left for immersive image and massive Year text. 40% Right for the editorial data column. DO NOT use generic dashboard cards. Use harsh 1px borders (border-white/10) to separate data points (Wins, Poles, Points) in a raw architectural grid.
grids.mobile: Single column stack. Image remains fixed in background, fading to solid black at the bottom. The massive year acts as a header. Content scrolls internally over the black bottom area.

layouts.architecture: A full-screen (100vh) locked container. It intercepts lateral navigation (keyboard/arrows) to change seasons without moving the global Lenis vertical scroll. Fixes the 'laggy on PC' issue completely by utilizing a virtualized state-driven rendering approach.
layouts.left_panel: Absolute positioning. Contains the synced season photograph, scaling down slowly via Framer Motion.
layouts.right_panel: Flex column, aligned right, h-full, pt-32 pb-12 pr-12. Contains the dynamically colored Championship Position title, the architectural stat grid, and the scrollable circuit achievements list.
layouts.circuit_list: Internal overflow-y-auto (hidden scrollbar, h-[40vh]). A sleek list of locations. Each row features track name, achievement (Win, Pod, Pole), and subtle hover state linked to the team's color.
layouts.navigation: A bottom-fixed horizontal timeline scrubber acting as a minimalist progress bar, alongside left/right control arrows.

motion.strategy: Wrap the main content in <AnimatePresence mode='wait'>. Only mount the data for the active year. Animate opacity and transform only.
motion.transitions: Images scale from 1.05 down to 1 while fading in over 0.8s. Data points stagger in from the bottom (translate-y-4) over 0.4s.
motion.performance: DO NOT animate height, width, or layout properties. Render ONLY the active year's DOM nodes. Preload images for next/prev years via standard Image object instantiation in a useEffect.

accessibility.keyboard: Implement useEffect to attach 'keydown' listeners for ArrowLeft and ArrowRight to navigate seasons.
accessibility.screen_reader: Add aria-live='polite' to the container holding the season data to announce the year change.
accessibility.contrast: Ensure the gradient overlay behind right-column text is fully opaque (#080808) at the far right to guarantee WCAG AA contrast.

media.image_strategy: Maintain a data array referencing the existing authentic photograph URLs per season. Apply CSS filter: grayscale(20%) contrast(110%) to unify the authentic photography into the dark editorial theme.

3d_libraries.usage: Use Framer Motion to create '2.5D' parallax (image moving independently from the typography). DO NOT inject a new Canvas or Three.js scene here, to avoid conflicting with the global Winding Racetrack R3F setup. Keep it strictly DOM-based and ultra-optimized.

image_urls.description: High speed F1 car on track

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. Replace the existing laggy vertical timeline with a new 100vh locked component at /app/frontend/src/components/TimelineChapter.js.
2. The root container MUST be `h-screen w-full relative overflow-hidden bg-[#080808]` to bypass the global Lenis scroll for this chapter.

3. Define a comprehensive array of data objects for seasons 2007-2025. Each object must include `year`, `team`, `championshipPosition`, `stats: { wins, podiums, poles, points }`, `image`, and an array of `circuits` (where he won/podiumed).
4. Manage active season via a `currentSeasonIndex` state. Implement keyboard ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to change it.
5. Render the left-aligned image inside `<AnimatePresence mode='wait'>` to smoothly transition. Cover it with an absolute gradient to merge into the right-side solid background.
6. Render the `year` in massive Unbounded font, clamped massively (e.g., text-[12vw]), anchored bottom-left over the image, with z-index 10.

7. On the right, create an editorial data panel. Map `championshipPosition` to the exact hex colors and glows defined in the guidelines. Apply the Team's CSS variable/color to navigation active states.
8. Build a harsh, border-based grid for the stats, dropping typical cards. Use text-white for numbers, text-white/50 for labels in Space Mono.

9. Create the `circuits` list inside a vertically scrollable div (`overflow-y-auto h-[40vh] scrollbar-none`). Every element must have a specific `data-testid` (e.g., `data-testid='timeline-prev-btn'`, `data-testid='circuit-row-monza'`).
10. Ensure the component is highly performant—only the currently active season's DOM elements should exist, with images gracefully fading.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic outputs. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) combined with solid borders.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy and varied opacities.
You MUST NOT apply universal transitions (e.g., transition: all). Specifically target opacity, transform, and background-color.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions. Static = dead.
Always add data-testid attributes to ALL interactive buttons, form inputs, and key informational elements.
Do not center align layouts generically; use asymmetrical tension (e.g., heavy left image, precise right grid).
DO NOT use complete transparent backgrounds behind text. Always provide a legible contrast base (scrim or blur).
